# following the "add this book" (?plusbook=) and venue-edit links to them, about 500 an hour
# (validateuser failure log, 2026-10-24). /addbooks also covers /addbooks.php and its fragments;

# A Disallow here would be counterproductive: a blocked URL is never fetched, so Google
# would never see the 404 and the URL would sit in the index indefinitely. The real LCC
# pages are /lcc and /lcc/{code} and are crawlable.

# robots.txt path matching is CASE-SENSITIVE, so this rule only ever matched the uppercase
# spelling. The site links, and the sitemap submits, the lowercase /mds/ form -- 150,000 codes
# across three ddc_new_*.xml.gz files -- so MDS was never actually blocked, which is just as
# well because it is meant to be indexed. The uppercase path serves the same page (200, no
# redirect), so the rule was blocking a duplicate nothing links. Kept, and now paired with a
# self-referencing canonical on the lowercase form in mds_controller.php. Reviewed 2026-09-19.
Disallow: /MDS/
Disallow: /readmessage.php*
Disallow: /search_works*
Disallow: /search*
Disallow: /title/
# Work pages: only the canonical /work/N/t/Slug form is crawlable. Longest rule wins,
# so Allow (/work/*/t/, 10 chars) beats Disallow (/work/, 6) and the per-work
# Disallow lines below (/work/NNNNNNNN, 14) still beat the Allow.
Allow: /work/*/t/

# /stats/ -- block REMOVED 2026-09-20, deliberately, and this needs explaining before anyone
# puts it back.
#
# Member stats pages should not be in the index (decided 2026-09-20). They were blocked here,
# and they are in the index anyway: /stats/unpetaling/overview, /stats/mb1066/genre,
# /stats/notion/ddc and more, all live in Google right now. That is not a contradiction -- a
# Disallow stops CRAWLING, not INDEXING. Google will hold a URL it found from links whether or
# not it may fetch it, and while the block stands it can never read a noindex, because it can
# never fetch the page. The block is what made the situation permanent.
#
# nstats_controller.php and yearinreview_controller.php now send noindex. For that to do
# anything, these pages have to be crawlable. Expect a period of extra crawl on ~1M members x
# ~20 stat types while Google reads the directive and drops them; once the index is clean the
# block can be restored if crawl budget matters, and at that point it will be doing its actual
# job (saving fetches) rather than freezing a bad state.
#

# REMOVED 2026-09-20: a `User-agent: bingbot` group containing only `Crawl-delay: 2`.
#
# A crawler obeys exactly ONE group -- the most specific one whose user-agent matches -- and
# ignores every other group, including `User-agent: *`. So naming bingbot here did not ADD a
# crawl delay to the site-wide rules; it gave Bing a group of its own with no Disallow lines in
# it, exempting Bing from ALL ~90 exclusions below: /ajax_*, /catalog.php, /catalog_resultset.php,
# the /a/ and /profile/ subpages, everything.
#
# The `Crawl-delay: 2` it contained is already in the `User-agent: *` group, so deleting the
# group loses nothing and restores the exclusions for Bing.
#
# Same mechanism applies to the `User-agent: Twitterbot` group at the top of this file, which is
# presumably deliberate (card fetching) -- but be aware it exempts Twitterbot from everything too.
